injuries.description: fracture of orbits and traumatic optic neuropathy
source: Amongst other injuries, the plaintiff suffered a fracture of orbits and traumatic optic neuropathy in the traffic accident on 8 December 2000
He had suffered from panhypopituitarism, a condition that occurs with severe frontal damage as the pituitary gland is situated on the frontal base of the skull.
The plaintiff developed Hypopituitarism and Cranial Diabetes Insipidus within days of the accident as can be seen from the reports of the Government hospitals.

injuries.description: persistent skull deformity; forehead was depressed due to the underlying frontal sinus fracture and previous cranioplasty
source: The plaintiff had persistent skull deformity. His forehead was depressed due to the underlying frontal sinus fracture and previous cranioplasty.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of squama of frontal bone of skull

injuries.description: reconstruction with ribs harvested from the chest and free Latissimus Dorsi flap with resulting scars on his back and weakened ability to pull because the muscle was harvested for reconstruction
injuries.body_part: left chest / back (latissimus dorsi donor site)
source: The skull defect was reconstructed by ribs harvested from the chest and the soft tissue coverage was achieved by a free Latissimus Dorsi flap. After the operation, the plaintiff was left with scars on his back and his ability to pull is weakened because the muscle was harvested for reconstruction.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at shoulder or upper arm level

source: In their joint report, they made the finding that the plaintiff was suffering from (1) Depressive Disorder; (2) Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD); and (3) Dementia due to Head Trauma.

For the Depressive Disorder, that manifests itself in the form of depressive mood, lack of interests energy and motivation, sleep impairment, retardation, restlessness, and feelings of worthlessness. The disorder is moderate in degree and is a psychological reaction to the accident and its physical and psychological consequences.

injuries.description: Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) (chronic, moderate to severe)
source: For the PTSD this is shown by his exposure to a traumatic event which threatened serious injury. It manifests itself in persistent re-experiencing of the traumatic event such as nightmares and flashback of the accident. ... The condition, having lasted more than three months, is now chronic and is moderate to severe.

injuries.description: Dementia due to Head Trauma (mild to moderate degree); associated Post Concussional Syndrome (headaches, dizziness)
source: The Dementia due to Head Trauma is shown by the plaintiff’s impairment of memory and executive functioning which results from very severe head injury from the accident and is mild to moderate in degree in that work and social activities are impaired but the capacity for independent living largely remains.
The Dementia as well as the headaches and dizziness of the PCS are permanent.

injuries.description: mild bilateral sixth nerve palsy (affecting horizontal eye movement)
source: As for his diplopia, Dr Choa takes the view that the plaintiff has a mild bilateral sixth nerve palsy which only controls horizontal eye movement.

manifestations.description: poor vision of his left eye
limitation of extraocular movement and visual impairment over his left eye
headaches mainly at the left frontal region occurring two to three times a week and lasting for two to three hours, associated with dizziness
diplopia at the extremes of lateral gaze horizontally
global cognitive dysfunction; severely lethargic and apathetic; slow and laboured responses; rarely spoke; took exceptionally long in dressing and bathing
suicidal ideas; severe depression; irritability and shouting at family members over trivial matters
CSF leakage from the nose and the right ear (which healed with conservative management)
right hand dorsum ulceration which required splintage
features of personality change in reaction to disfigurement with feelings of inadequacy, social ineptness and hypersensitivity, avoidance of social activities and interpersonal relationships

treatments_received.treatment: Exploration of the forehead wound, surgical toilet and repair of the finger tendon
source: Exploration of the forehead wound, surgical toilet and repair of the finger tendon were performed on the same day.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Tendon repair / Suture of tendon of hand

treatments_received.treatment: Craniotomy, evacuation of the epidural haematoma and fixation of the skull bone fragments by mini-plates
source: As a result, Craniotomy, evacuation of the epidural haematoma and fixation of the skull bone fragments by mini-plates were carried out on the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: Reopening of the craniotomy and left orbitotomy as well as decompression and repair of dural tear (14 December 2000)
source: Reopening of the craniotomy and left orbitotomy as well as decompression and repair of dural tear were performed on 14 December 2000

treatments_received.treatment: Wound debridement and rotational flap and free skin graft from the left side of his neck (5 January 2001)
source: Wound debridement and rotational flap and free skin graft from the left side of his neck were performed on 5 January 2001.

treatments_received.treatment: Wound exploration and debridement, craniectomy and removal of the necrotic bone and plates as well as drainage of the epidural abscess (2 April 2001)
source: Wound exploration and debridement, craniectomy and removal of the necrotic bone and plates as well as drainage of the epidural abscess were performed on 2 April 2001.

treatments_received.treatment: Insertion of a subclavian line under local anaesthesia for venous access; prolonged course of antibiotics
source: A subclavian line was inserted under local anaesthesia on 19 April for venous access and prolonged course of antibiotics was prescribed.

treatments_received.treatment: Skull reconstruction: ribs harvested from the chest and free Latissimus Dorsi flap (9 October 2002)
source: The skull defect was reconstructed by ribs harvested from the chest and the soft tissue coverage was achieved by a free Latissimus Dorsi flap.
A subclavian line was inserted under local anaesthesia on 19 April for venous access and prolonged course of antibiotics was prescribed.

treatments_received.treatment: Hormonal replacement (hydrocortisone, thyroxine, testosterone, desmopressin) as required for pituitary failure
source: The government medical reports show that the plaintiff requires medication for the treatment of hypofunction of the adrenal glands, thyroid, testes and posterior pituitary (known as Cranial Diabetes Insipidus).
The plaintiff will need lifelong hormonal replacement as recovery is very unusual.

treatments_received.treatment: Regular ophthalmology follow up every three months
source: Amongst other injuries, the plaintiff suffered a fracture of orbits and traumatic optic neuropathy in the traffic accident on 8 December 2000 and is still attending regular follow up treatment at the Department of Ophthalmology of Caritas Medical Centre every three months.

treatments_future.treatment: Psychotherapy and medication (psychiatric treatment for around two years)
source: My reading of their joint report indicates that the psychiatric treatment recommended is for two years and not five, as submitted by plaintiff’s counsel.
In view of the age of the plaintiff, and that the endocrine treatment and replacement is lifelong, I have no hesitation in adopting the multiplier of 18 as suggested by the plaintiff.

Accordingly, the cost of the future endocrinologists consultations is assessed at $54,000; the Testosterone replacement at $86,400 and for the Hydrocortisone, Thyroxine and Desmopressin medication at $486,000

treatments_future.treatment: Hydrocortisone, Thyroxine and Desmopressin medication (future lifelong replacement)
source: Accordingly, the cost of the future endocrinologists consultations is assessed at $54,000; the Testosterone replacement at $86,400 and for the Hydrocortisone, Thyroxine and Desmopressin medication at $486,000

treatments_future.treatment: Growth Hormone replacement (possible in next 10-15 years)
source: In a further report dated 22 June 2005, Dr Chang confirmed that in the case of the plaintiff, there is no evidence of Growth Hormone deficiency as he has normal IGF-1 when assessed in November 2004. However there is a high chance that he may develop Growth Hormone deficiency in future and this can only be confirmed by periodic (yearly) testing of IGF-1.
Taking all the above into account, the multiplier of assessing the Growth Hormone replacement will need to be trimmed down from 18 to one of 9 in all the circumstances.

treatments_future.treatment: Infertility treatment with hormones (future cost estimated at $200,000)
source: There is also a claim for infertility treatment with hormones the cost of which was estimated at $200,000 by Dr Chang.

losses.description: Poor vision especially left eye with generalized visual field constriction and defective colour vision; combined visual disability assessed as 42% impairment of the whole visual system (40% whole person).

Readily noticeable pale accident scars over much of his forehead; conspicuous raised skin flap on left forehead; scars on back from donor site; noticeable scars on wrist, hand and neck; cosmetic disability permanent.
Weakened ability to pull because the Latissimus Dorsi muscle was harvested for reconstruction.

Features of personality change in reaction to his disfigurement with feelings of inadequacy, social ineptness and hypersensitivity, sense of humiliation and discrimination and fear of embarrassment, ridicule, criticism and rejection.
Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the accident, avoidance of minibuses, going out alone, avoidance of social activities and interpersonal relationships; coldness to family members.
Work and social activities are impaired by cognitive dysfunction and dementia which affects capacity for employment and functioning in the labour market.

losses.category: Loss of ability to participate in parenthood or grandparenthood
losses.description: Gonadal hormone deficiency resulting in loss of libido, masculinity and infertility; infertility treatment claimed.
